groups.title: Component Model
groups.question: You are building a Svelte 5 card component with a title prop, a like count and a slot for custom content. Explain how components, runes and composition work.

followUps.Single-file components and props declara: How is a Svelte component structured and how are props declared in Svelte 5?
followUps.Slots and component composition patterns: How does a parent pass custom markup into a child component?

evidence.text: A .svelte file has script, markup and style sections.
Svelte 5 declares props with the $props rune.
Props flow from parent to child.
$state makes a variable reactive, so changes update the UI.
$derived computes a value from other state and updates automatically.
Runes make reactive data flow explicit and are handled by the compiler.
Slots, or snippets in Svelte 5, let a parent pass markup into a child.
This is how layout wrappers like cards and modals are built.
Several named slots or snippets let the parent fill different areas.

groups.title: Template Directives
groups.question: You render a todo list that can be reordered and an empty-state message. Explain how Svelte's template blocks work.

followUps.Conditional rendering with if and else b: What does {#if} do to the DOM?
followUps.List rendering with each blocks and keys: Why add a key to an {#each} block?

evidence.text: {#if} includes or removes markup based on a condition.
Svelte creates and destroys the real DOM elements, not a virtual copy.
{:else} handles the alternative case, like an empty state.
{#each} repeats markup for each item.
A key tells Svelte which item is which.
With keys, reordering moves elements correctly instead of mixing up their state.

groups.title: Events and Bindings
groups.question: You are building a search form whose input updates state and whose button triggers a search. Explain events and bindings in Svelte 5.

followUps.DOM event handling with onclick and on d: How do you handle a click in Svelte 5?

evidence.text: Svelte 5 uses onclick as a normal attribute with a handler.
The handler is a function that runs when the event fires.
Svelte may delegate some events to a shared listener for performance.
bind:value keeps an input and a state variable in sync both ways.
It removes the need to write an input handler.
It suits common form inputs like text fields and checkboxes.

groups.title: Styles and Scoping
groups.question: A component's .title style unexpectedly does not affect a child component, and you need an active tab style. Explain how styling works in Svelte.

followUps.Scoped CSS and global style overrides: Why don't a component's styles affect other components?
followUps.Class and style directives for dynamic s: How do class: and style: directives help with dynamic styling?

evidence.text: Styles in a component's style block are scoped to that component.
Svelte adds a unique class to keep them from leaking.
The :global() modifier is used when a style must reach outside.
class:active={isActive} adds the class only when the condition is true.
style:color={value} sets an inline style reactively.
This avoids building class strings by hand.
